headline: Long-term holders sold at an average 18% loss on Nov 9, short-term holders at 1%: the loss-taking has moved to last year's top buyers.
summary: The coins taking losses this week have been held for over a year: LTH-SOPR dropped to 0.82 in a day while short-term holders sold near break-even. Miners are squeezed too, with hashrate down 9% in a week and difficulty set to drop about 7% on Nov 13. The 75,253 close sits between the 200-day average at 73,156 and short-term holder cost at 75,852, and tonight's CPI (08:30 ET) is the week's first test.

overview.lead: The source of selling has changed: long-term holders who bought near last year's highs are handing over coins at a loss, while short-term holders and leverage haven't left.
points: Long-term holders sold at an average 18% loss on Nov 9; short-term holders lost under 1% (see finding one).
Miner revenue fell by a quarter in a week while price fell only 4.5%; the gap is slower blocks (see finding two).
Leverage came straight back: three-venue funding went from 6.5% to 8.2% in a day, and open interest rose 1%.
US stocks jumped 2.7% on Nov 9 and BTC rose only 0.7%; CPI tonight, PPI Friday.

cycle.lead: Bull phase day 32, and the cycle gauges keep weakening: the weekly bull-bear score fell to 0.14, one step from flipping bearish.
points: The close has been above a rising 200-day average for 61 days; bull day 32.
Only 1 of 6 evidence lights is on (realized cap growth); 12-month momentum, MVRV vs its 1-year mean, exchange supply, short-term holder cost and cost vs the True Market Mean are all off.
The weekly bull-bear score went 0.23 → 0.14, still early bull; the Dawn Index is at Daybreak with heat 37. The score tracks trend and heat tracks valuation, and both lean weak.
At the last 30 days' pace, a straight-line extrapolation puts short-term holder cost crossing above the True Market Mean near Dec 13.

market.lead: Monday's intraday low of 73,602 touched the swing end line at 73,605 almost exactly before the close recovered to 75,253; that line and the 200-day average sit within 3% below.
points: The bounce had volume: 1.33x the 20-day average, closing at 87% of the day's range.
Selling pressure has been at 100 for 3 days with momentum quality 0.27, so the bottom combo is still on (in 21 past cases, price fell a median 9% more during the combo).
The close is at the 44th percentile of the past year's closes, with the 1-year median of 76,947 just 2% above.

deriv.lead: Sunday's liquidations didn't push leverage out, and longs added back on Monday's bounce; dealer hedging pins price near 75,000, and a break below 74,000 is where moves can accelerate.
points: Open interest is 342,441 BTC, up 1% in a day and still at the 98th percentile since 2021; 73.7% of Binance accounts are long (Coinalyze).
Five-venue weighted funding is 9.8%, with Binance and Hyperliquid near 11%; against Nov 8 use the three-venue basis, 6.5% → 8.2%.

Estimated dealer gamma is positive at 75,000 (they sell rallies and buy dips, so price tends to stick) and turns negative at 74,000 (Deribit only); the estimated long liquidation band is 72.2–73.3K, 3.4% below the close (estimate, seven venues).
The implied volatility curve went from inverted back to flat (7-day 38.5%, 90-day 38.7%), so the weekend panic premium is gone; the 25-delta risk reversal is −3.0, puts still richer.

flows.lead: US money is still leaving: Coinbase spot net sold 2,882 BTC in a week, in the heaviest 5% since 2021, and ETFs and stablecoins haven't turned.
points: ETF outflows of $1.36B over 7 trading days (to Nov 5, The Block); Nov 6 provisionally another −$412M, Nov 9 not yet published.
Stablecoins at $293.0B, down $13B in 30 days.
The Coinbase premium is −0.145% daily and −0.139% on a 7-day average, so US buying is still at a discount; spot taker buying on Binance turned slightly positive for the week.
Realized cap is +0.31% over 30 days, so money is still trickling in; it's the only evidence light that's on.

onchain.lead: The losses are concentrated in old coins: STH-SOPR at 0.992 is a small loss, LTH-SOPR at 0.82 a heavy one, and a third of 30-day realized losses came from coins held 1–2 years.
points: This page's finding: long-term holder loss-taking deepened in a day, but the dollar amount is still under half of this cycle's three earlier lows (see finding one).
Only 29% of short-term holders are in profit; their realized loss was 4,007 BTC, a little higher than the day before and far from the 5,000 capitulation line (CheckOnChain, Nov 9).

Network-wide daily profit/loss has been below 0.35 for 4 days, with a 7-day average of 0.60; at that pace the 90-day average falls back below 1 around Jan 4 (in Dec 2019 it also slipped back below 1 after seven months above).
Apparent demand is −259K BTC over 30 days, still below its own 30-day average of −104K.

news.title: BTC fell to 73,761 late Sunday, its lowest since August, then bounced back above 75,000; over $1B of crypto positions were liquidated in 24 hours, $913M of them longs
news.read: The liquidations were mostly ETH ($448M); BTC was only $272M. Across our five venues, Nov 9 BTC long liquidations were just $28.8M, and open interest rose 1%. Leverage wasn't flushed, and the liquidation band near 72K is still there. No change to the market phase.

news.title: US October CPI is due Nov 10; Dow Jones consensus is +0.3% m/m headline and +0.2% core; no annual rate will be published because of last year's shutdown data gap; FedWatch puts a December hike above 80%
news.read: A December hike is already over 80% priced, so a hot print would take out the rest and put real yields (10-year 2.63%) back under pressure; a soft one helps risk assets. BTC's 30-day correlation with the Nasdaq is 0.75. An event risk, not a cycle call.

news.title: US stocks rebounded: Nasdaq +2.74%, S&P 500 +2.35%, led by chipmakers; Nvidia fell 4.27% to $178.67 on the probe into its CEO
news.read: On a big up day for stocks BTC rose only 0.7%: it follows the drops but not the rallies, and US buying is still at a discount (Coinbase 7-day average −0.139%). Monday's rebound is outside support for BTC and doesn't change the on-chain or cycle readings.

news.title: US spot BTC ETFs had $1.282B of net outflows last week, the most since late June, with four of five days negative; 2026 year-to-date flows are now −$914M
news.read: Matches our data: ETF outflows of $1.36B over 7 trading days (to Nov 5, The Block). Year-to-date flows that turned positive in September are negative again, and this US money channel hasn't come back. No change to the market phase.

news.title: Strategy bought $81.9M of BTC at an average $79,012 during Nov 2–8, for an average cost of $75,456, funded by common stock sales
news.read: The purchase is about one-fifteenth of last week's ETF outflow and can't hold price up; the 75,253 close is still below its cost. The same stock sales also funded a $188.3M preferred buyback, more than the BTC buy. No change to the cycle call.

news.title: mempool.space projects a −6.4% next difficulty adjustment, the biggest cut since June; hashrate is about 963 EH/s with a 3-day average of 903, suggesting some machines are switching off
news.read: Our estimate from the same source as of Nov 10 is −7.14%, with the 7-day average hashrate down 9.2% in a week (see finding two). Squeezed miners may sell, but Hash Ribbons show no capitulation cross yet. No change to the cycle call.

news.title: Brent fell 5.5% to $92.96 as Iran reviewed Qatar's mediation proposals and Trump called renewed strikes "highly unlikely"; Secretary of State Rubio said talks had stalled
news.read: Oil was above $112 at the start of the month; the drop helps inflation and rate expectations and leans positive for BTC, but BTC hasn't benefited this week, with stablecoins still down $13B in 30 days. No change to the cycle call.

findings.title: Those taking losses bought one to two years ago; short-term traders aren't capitulating
findings.lean_why: The sellers are old coins stuck at high prices, and roughly 800K long-term holder coins sit underwater in the 84K band, so rebounds there meet their break-even selling; short-term holders haven't capitulated, so the handover below isn't done either.
findings.what: Who is selling into this drop: long-term holders sold at an average 18% loss on Nov 9 (LTH-SOPR 0.82), while short-term holders lost under 1% (STH-SOPR 0.992). The deepest losses are coins bought near the 2025 highs that have now passed 155 days (Bitview, CheckOnChain, Nov 9).
findings.why: The question is who is selling at 75K, and split by holder group the two sides behave in opposite ways. 36% of 30-day realized losses came from coins held 1–2 years, up from 29% 30 days ago, while the 6–12 month group fell from 23% to 11% (Bitview). The cost map fits: long-term holders' overall cost is 48,796 and deep in profit, but about 800K of their coins sit in the 84K band, 12% above the close (CheckOnChain, Nov 9). Behavior agrees: the LTH-SOPR 7-day average is 0.94 and has dropped 42% in 30 days, while long-term holders' 30-day net position is −69K BTC and narrowing, so the volume sold is modest but those selling are losing a lot. On the short-term side, realized losses of 4,007 BTC are far from June's capitulation, and STH-SOPR has been below 1 for 4 days but only at 0.992.
findings.alt: LTH-SOPR is a single-day reading; one large move of old coins (an exchange or custodian consolidating wallets) can drag it down, and per-UTXO data can't tell internal transfers apart. The 7-day average of 0.94 is much milder. Part of the rise in the 1–2 year group is coins bought at the late-2024 highs just turning one year old. Bitview and CheckOnChain are different vendors, so only directions are compared.
findings.history: At this cycle's three lows, long-term holders' weekly realized loss was 0.2–0.3% of market cap (Nov 22 2025, Feb 5 2026, Jun 30 2026); now it is 0.1%, or $1.5B (Bitview, Nov 9). In the two bear markets before 2022 the largest loss came at the bottom; 2022 was the exception, with only four cycles of data.
findings.so: The chain of logic: old coins have started selling at a loss, so the trapped supply at 76–86K is the main resistance for rebounds; short-term holders haven't capitulated and the loss is still under half of earlier lows, so seller exhaustion isn't established. At a 70,000 close, long-term holders at a paper loss would rise from 5.69M to 6.09M BTC, and to 6.78M at 66,000 (CheckOnChain estimate table); the increase is slow above 66K, supply there is thin, and price tends to move fast through it.
findings.next: Two paths by Nov 16: long-term holders' weekly realized loss above $2.5B means old-coin capitulation is spreading toward the size of this cycle's earlier lows, which confirms; the LTH-SOPR 7-day average back at 1 or above means old coins have stopped selling at a loss and this was a few large moves, which refutes.

findings.title: Hashrate down 9% in a week; miner revenue cut by a quarter
findings.lean_why: Squeezed miners may be forced to sell in the short run, but low Puell readings have historically sat near bottoms, and hashrate leaving plus a difficulty cut return the remaining miners to profit; the two sides offset.
findings.what: Miner revenue dropped sharply in a week, mostly from slower blocks rather than price: the Puell multiple fell from 1.00 to 0.76, a 7-day drop in the largest 2% of the past year, while price fell only 4.5% over the same week (CoinMetrics Nov 8, mempool.space Nov 9).
findings.why: Puell is miners' daily dollar revenue divided by its 1-year average. Price went only from 78,239 to 74,738 between Nov 1 and Nov 8; the rest of the drop came from block production. The 7-day average hashrate fell from 1,069 to 970 EH/s and the average block time stretched to 646 seconds (target 600), so fewer coins are mined per day at the same difficulty. Fees are only 0.9% of revenue and can't fill the gap. A second source shows the same thing: mempool.space's 3-day average hashrate is only 903 EH/s, read as some machines powering down (24/7 Wall St.). Hash Ribbons haven't crossed (30-day 1,035, 60-day 997), so the miner capitulation signal is off.
findings.alt: Block times involve luck, and a one-week hashrate estimate can be off by more than 5%; Puell uses daily values, and once difficulty drops an estimated 7.14% on Nov 13, block times return to normal and revenue recovers. Breakeven estimates vary widely: a 20 J/TH machine at $0.06 power breaks even at 61,528, an older 25 J/TH one at 89,729, so only the less efficient fleet is losing money.
findings.history: After a sharp weekly fall in miner revenue, things usually didn't get worse. It has happened only 2 times since Nov 2023 (both in June 2025), with 30-day returns of +3.1% and +12.6%, against a +1.4% median for any day.
findings.so: What changed is miner supply: inefficient miners are being squeezed out and short-term selling pressure rises, though the amount is small (about 450 new BTC a day). The cycle readings didn't change: Hash Ribbons show no capitulation, and the market phase and exit framework are unchanged.
findings.next: Two paths by Nov 16: the 7-day average hashrate falling below 940 EH/s means shutdowns are spreading and may lead to a Hash Ribbons capitulation, which confirms the miner squeeze; a return above 1,030 EH/s means this week was bad block luck, which refutes.

research.summary: Glassnode's Nov 9 Market Pulse agrees with our readings: ETF outflows, short-term holders slightly underwater, crowded longs. It says selling pressure is starting to fade; we see one more thing, that the main loss-takers are now long-term holders. K33's latest is still Nov 2, and no new weekly from The Block Research or Coinbase Institutional was found.

items.title: BTC Market Pulse: Week 46
items.points: BTC near 75K, closing at its lowest since August; spot CVD −$91.8M; futures OI $37.0B, down only 1.1%, with long funding payments still above the high band; 25-delta skew 11.1%, strong demand for downside protection; weekly ETF outflows $1.6B and ETF MVRV 1.30, below its low band; short-term holders slipped into a small unrealized loss on Sunday; realized P/L ratio −0.63. Conclusion: defensive positioning and crowded longs, but some leverage has been flushed and momentum no longer confirms the decline.
items.meaning: "Crowded longs" matches our data (open interest at the 98th percentile, 73.7% of Binance accounts long), but we see leverage added back on Nov 9, so "some leverage flushed" doesn't hold yet. Its $1.6B weekly ETF outflow and SoSoValue's $1.28B use different definitions.

items.title: The Week On-chain: Idling at Support
items.points: True Market Mean 77.7K, short-term holder cost 75.7K, with the 200-day average inside a 73–76K band; long liquidation risk at 73–76K and 60–63K; holding 73–76K is a healthy reset, while a break below 73K points to longer consolidation.
items.meaning: The Nov 9 intraday low of 73,602 touched the band's lower edge and recovered; the 75,253 close is still inside. Its "below 73K" nearly coincides with our hedge line at 73,156.

items.title: Another resilience test: The Midterms are here
items.points: Public preview: CME open interest at a three-year low, perpetual leverage rising, BTC near key support, with a meaningful chance of a large move after the election.
items.meaning: Preview only, not used for judgment; high perpetual leverage still holds on Nov 9 (open interest 342,441 BTC).

items.title: BTC Market Pulse: Week 45
